text:
I recently used my social security benefits a few days ago. The counter staff asked if I was using my social security benefits, and I said yes. ***This is considered normal practice at the counter.***
(I had already inquired about the cost, which was approximately 900-1200 baht). Before seeing the doctor, the doctor also asked, ***"Are you using your social security benefits?"*** I replied yes, but I was wondering why the doctor needed to know whether I was using them or not.
This led me to question:
1. If I didn't mention that I was using my benefits, what would the service cost be? Would it be more or less than the budget provided by the Social Security Office?
2. Does the care or service differ whether I use or don't use my benefits? And why did the doctor ask?
3. If I said I was using my benefits, regardless of the severity of the oral health problem, the full 1200 baht coverage would still apply. Wouldn't I still have to pay extra? So, I still had to add another 300.
*In summary, as suspected, it was the full 1200 baht, with a difference of 300 baht. But the counter charged another 50 baht for something I don't know what, because initially we agreed it wouldn't exceed 1200 baht. The total was 1250 baht, so I had to add another 350 baht anyway. I was confused about what the extra charge was for, but I didn't want to know because I was in a hurry, so I just paid and left quickly because I had other business to attend to. Before I left, the counter staff asked if I wanted to schedule a next service appointment (I thought to myself, "Maybe not yet"). I think this will probably be a one-time thing.
